summary: Security-fix regression pass on BSA GRC (Next.js). Ran 15 pytest cases covering admin login, MCP token lifecycle (hash storage, prefix-only listing, revoke/reactivate/delete, MCP API auth), blog markdown link renderer, XSS sanitization of body, media proxy prefix restriction, and admin image upload. Also UI-verified /admin/mcp shows only masked token prefixes (bsagrc_mcp_xxxx...••••) with no reveal button, Cabut/Hapus actions available, and hermes token preserved. 14/15 passed. Discovered ONE NEW stored XSS vulnerability outside the fixed markdown pipeline: excerpt/keywords/description are inlined into ' – payload appears raw in DOM outside the LD-JSON script). Same unsafe pattern exists in 5 other pages but only [slug]/page.tsx blog view uses user-controlled fields today.

critical.issue: STORED XSS in JSON-LD structured data. app/[slug]/page.tsx lines 88-89 render ' in the excerpt breaks out of the script tag and executes as HTML in the visitor's/admin's browser. Reproduced: created blog with excerpt='' — payload appears raw in returned HTML at the boundary. Same pattern exists (but with non-user data currently) in app/layout.tsx, app/page.tsx, app/layanan/[slug]/page.tsx, app/portofolio/[id]/page.tsx.

action_items: Fix stored XSS in JSON-LD: sanitize the stringified schema before injection. Simplest fix in app/[slug]/page.tsx (and the other 4 files as defense-in-depth): replace `JSON.stringify(schema)` with `JSON.stringify(schema).replace(/</g, '\\u003c').replace(/>/g, '\\u003e').replace(/&/g, '\\u0026')` or use a helper like `serialize-javascript`. This is the standard mitigation for JSON embedded in <script> blocks. Do NOT rely on sanitize-html in lib/markdown.ts here — that only cleans the rendered HTML body, not the SEO metadata block.
Consider running the sanitize-html allowlist on excerpt/keywords BEFORE they are used for SEO fields too, or strip HTML tags entirely from excerpt/keywords before persistence.
critical_code_review_comments: app/[slug]/page.tsx lines 88-89: JSON.stringify inside dangerouslySetInnerHTML without escaping '</' – classic JSON-in-script XSS sink. Same anti-pattern in 4 sibling files.
app/api/admin/blog/route.ts: excerpt auto-derived from body.content.slice(0,160) preserves raw HTML/script tags; recommend stripping tags before storing OR at rendering time when used as description.
Positive: lib/tokens.ts hashing (SHA-256), constant-time compare, tokenPrefix-only listing, and TokenPrefixValue component are all cleanly implemented; UI has no reveal path for stored tokens.
Positive: media proxy prefix restriction is effective (all non-'bsa-grc/' paths return 404) and did NOT break existing blob-served images or new uploads.
Positive: markdown link renderer now emits proper anchor with maroon-600 (external) / maroon-700 (internal) styling and did not regress headings, tables, lists, bold.

rca of the issue.bug: Stored XSS via JSON-LD structured data in blog article pages.
rca of the issue.root_cause: app/[slug]/page.tsx builds `articleSchema` from user-controllable blog fields (title, excerpt, keywords) and injects it into the DOM via `<script type="application/ld+json" dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: JSON.stringify(articleSchema) }} />`. JSON.stringify does not escape the substring '</' inside JSON strings; therefore any string field containing the literal '</script>' terminates the outer <script> tag in the HTML parser and the remainder is parsed as HTML.
rca of the issue.reproduction: 1) POST /api/admin/blog (or /api/mcp/blog with a blog:write token) with body {"title":"x","slug":"x","content":"safe","excerpt":"","isPublished":true}. 2) GET /x. 3) The payload appears verbatim in the DOM and the injected onerror handler executes for any visitor (including admins).
rca of the issue.mitigation: Escape the JSON before inlining: `const safeJson = JSON.stringify(schema).replace(/</g, '\\u003c').replace(/>/g, '\\u003e').replace(/&/g, '\\u0026').replace(/\u2028/g, '\\u2028').replace(/\u2029/g, '\\u2029');` then use that in dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Apply to all five files that use this pattern. Additionally, strip HTML tags from excerpt/keywords server-side before storage.
rca of the issue.severity: HIGH — same practical impact as the original stored-XSS finding (auth cookie theft, admin session hijack when a superuser previews the article), and reachable by exactly the same actor (MCP blog:write token holder or any admin editor).
